```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# code to troublesheet file path issues. 
# By default, knitr uses the folder containing the .Rmd file as
# the working directory. This code allows us to set the folder
# with our .rProj in it as the root. 

# find_root looks upwards from the .Rmd until it finds a file or
# folder that matches the criteria "folder with a .Rproj file in
# it."

knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::is_rstudio_project))
```

## Load packages 
```{r message = false}
# load packages from the "libraries" script in the scripts folder
source("scripts/libraries.R")
```

## Pull in core metadata
```{r, echo = FALSE}
# echo = FALSE shows chunk output but not code. 

# read in bulk density data
bulk_density <- read_excel("data/bulk_density_export_from_sent_to_flett_20250602_saved_20250909.xlsx") %>%
  rename(bd = `bulk_density_g/cm3`)

# read in the metadata for each lake's sed core and add the bd values to each metadata df
TRK_metadata <- read_excel("data/0_TRK2_core_metadata_20250726.xlsx")  %>%  # read excel file
  select(lake_name:depth_bottom) %>%  # keep only the first few columns
  left_join(bulk_density %>%  # make a new df combining the metadata with bulk_density
              select(sample_ID, bd),  # select only these columns from bulk_density
            by = "sample_ID") # merge the two by sample_ID

  # left join: combines columns from TRK_metadata with the selected columns from bulk_density
  # and merges by "sample_ID". "left" means all rows in TRK_metadata are kept and data from 
  # bulk_density is added if a given row has a "sample_ID" in TRK_metadata. If the sample_ID 
  # doesn't match it gets dropped; if a sample_ID is not in bulk_density, it gets bd = NA. 
  
UFM_metadata <- read_excel("data/0_UFM1_core_metadata_20250726.xlsx") %>% 
  select(lake_name:depth_bottom) %>%
  left_join(bulk_density %>% 
              select(sample_ID, bd),
            by = "sample_ID")

LFM_metadata <- read_excel("data/0_LFM2_core_metadata_20250726.xlsx") %>% 
  select(lake_name:depth_bottom) %>%
  left_join(bulk_density %>% 
              select(sample_ID, bd),
            by = "sample_ID")
```

#Stable isotopes

```{r, echo = FALSE}
    
# Step One: pull in and clean up the IRMS run info. 

# NOTE: these files (SIA_run1_...SIA_run2_) still contains triplicates!
SIA_run1_TRK_UFM <- read_excel("data/TRK_UFM_SIA_data_clean_20250726.xlsx") %>%
  rename(sample_ID = Identifier1) %>% # rename column Identifier1 to sample_ID
  select(sample_ID, d13C.scale, percent.C, perC.drift, d15N.scale, percent.N) %>% 
  # pull in the %C, %N, d15N, and d13C columns recommended by the SIA lab based on the 
  # instrument diagnostics. percent.C and perC.drift were similar so we'll look at both. 
  mutate("C.drift:N" = perC.drift/percent.N, # make new columns calculating C:N both ways
         "C:N" = percent.C/percent.N) %>%
  rename(d13C = d13C.scale,
         d15N = d15N.scale)

# For now, inlcude both “perC.drift” AND "percent.C" for %C since a very small drift was detected in the HOS lin.std (this was within the error of 0.3% - where std.dev. was of multiple HOS standard replicates). 

# For manuscript: calculate C:N using both versions and see how errors propogate. 
# In thesis: use percent.C until have a reason not to.

# read in Run 2 with the corrected columns preferred for that run. 
SIA_run2_TRK_LFM <- 
  read_excel("data/TRK_LFM_SIA_data_clean_20250921.xlsx") %>%
    rename(sample_ID = Identifier1) %>%
    select(sample_ID, d13C.scale, linKpercent.C, d15N.scale, perN.drift) %>%
# standardize SIA column names across runs regardless of corrections used...
    rename(d13C = d13C.scale,
           percent.C = linKpercent.C, 
           d15N = d15N.scale,
           percent.N = perN.drift) %>%
    mutate("C:N" = percent.C/percent.N)

# Step Two: collapse triplicate values, and create a separate SI spreadsheet for each core (in format: metadata, SIA)

# Two a) join dataframes and keep all the observations in TRK_metadata (left, while throwing out any observations from SIA_run1_TRK_UFM, right, that don't have a sample_ID matching those in TRK_metadata). Right now that throws out UFM SIA, but keeps all the extra observations in the left database (e.g. TRK2_001, TRK2_002, TRK2_003...5, 7, 9)

TRK_SIA <- left_join(TRK_metadata, SIA_run1_TRK_UFM, by = "sample_ID") %>%
  select(-perC.drift, -"C.drift:N") # drop the C.drift columns for thesis

# Two b) create an object with row TRK2_002 from SIA_run2 to add to the data from run 1 later
row_TRK2_002_SIA <- SIA_run2_TRK_LFM %>%
  filter(sample_ID == "TRK2_002") %>%
  left_join(TRK_metadata, by = "sample_ID") %>%
  relocate(all_of(c(
    "lake_name",
    "core_number",
    "sample_ID",
    "sample_range",
    "depth_top",
    "depth_bottom",
    "d13C",
    "percent.C",
    "d15N",
    "percent.N",
    "C:N"
  ))) # keep columns in the same order.

# Two c) do regular cleaning (drop NA values and collapse triplicates)
TRK_SIA <- TRK_SIA %>%
    drop_na() %>% # drop all TRK samples for which we did not run SIA
    group_by(lake_name, core_number, sample_ID, sample_range, depth_top, depth_bottom, bd) %>% # add a step to run the summarize fn on groups of rows (each row could be grouped just by sample_ID, but output would then not include the other metadata; bc metadata should stay the same for duplicate samples, we can use this shortcut). 
    summarize(across(d13C:"C:N", ~mean(.x, na.rm=TRUE)), .groups = "keep") # summarize collapses rows--this fn will take the average of all the triplicates for every row (grouped by the columns above). ".x" is tidyverse's way of saying insert the line before right here when you choose what to take the mean of.

# Two d) add row TRK2_002 back in
TRK_SIA <- bind_rows(TRK_SIA, row_TRK2_002_SIA)

# Repeat step 2, but now create a UFM stable isotope file. 
UFM_SIA <- left_join(UFM_metadata, SIA_run1_TRK_UFM, by = "sample_ID") %>%
    select(-perC.drift, -"C.drift:N")

# take avg of triplicates
UFM_SIA <- UFM_SIA %>%
    drop_na() %>%
    group_by(lake_name, core_number, sample_ID, sample_range, depth_top, depth_bottom, bd) %>%
    summarize(across(d13C:"C:N", ~mean(.x, na.rm=TRUE)), .groups = "keep")
  
# create an LFM stable isotope file.
LFM_SIA <- left_join(LFM_metadata, SIA_run2_TRK_LFM, by = "sample_ID") %>%
  drop_na() %>%
  group_by(lake_name, core_number, sample_ID, sample_range, depth_top, depth_bottom, bd) %>%
  summarize(across(d13C:"C:N", ~mean(.x, na.rm=TRUE)), .groups = "keep")

# clean up Environment: 
rm(row_TRK2_002_SIA)
```

# Pigments
### Pull in pigment data
```{r}

# all raw pigment data is in the units nmol pigment / g total dry mass, so code below adds the suffix "_nmol_gDM". 

UFM_pigments_raw <- read_excel("data/UFM_final_HPLC_20250910.xlsx") %>% 
  select(depth_top, chlide_a:diadino, myxo:car_z) %>%
  rename(b_car = "b-car") %>% 
  rename_with(~paste0(.x, "_nmol_gDM"), .cols = c(chlide_a:car_z))

LFM_pigments_raw <- read_excel("data/LFM_final_HPLC_20250910.xlsx") %>% 
  select(depth_top, chlide_a:diadino, myxo:car_z) %>%
  rename(b_car = "b-car") %>% 
  rename_with(~paste0(.x, "_nmol_gDM"), .cols = c(chlide_a:car_z))

TRK_pigments_raw <- read_excel("data/TRK_final_HPLC_20250910.xlsx") %>% 
  select(depth_top, chlide_a:diadino, myxo:car_z) %>%
  rename(b_car = "b-car") %>% 
  rename_with(~paste0(.x, "_nmol_gDM"), .cols = c(chlide_a:car_z))

# glimpse(UFM_pigments_raw) # 31 pigments total!

```

### Join pigment and SIA dfs
```{r}
# join pigment and sia dfs for each core and add a depth_plot column 
# (= middle depth of each slice)

UFM_wide <- left_join(UFM_SIA, UFM_pigments_raw, by = "depth_top") %>%
  mutate(depth_plot = depth_top + 0.25) %>%
  relocate(depth_plot, .after = depth_bottom)

TRK_wide <- left_join(TRK_SIA, TRK_pigments_raw, by = "depth_top") %>%
  mutate(depth_plot = depth_top + 0.25) %>%
  relocate(depth_plot, .after = depth_bottom)

TRK_wide <- TRK_wide %>% # move row TRK2_002 to the top of the df
  arrange(desc(sample_ID == "TRK2_002"))

LFM_wide <- left_join(LFM_SIA, LFM_pigments_raw, by = "depth_top") %>%
  mutate(depth_plot = depth_top + 0.25) %>%
  relocate(depth_plot, .after = depth_bottom)

# glimpse(UFM_wide)
```

### Normalize pigment data in terms of total carbon / sample 
```{r}
# to go from nmoles pigment / g total dry mass to nmoles pigment / g TC (total carbon):  
# multiply by 100/percent.C, and add label _nmol_gTC

UFM_wide <- UFM_wide %>%
  mutate(across(ends_with("_nmol_gDM"), # for all the columns that end in _nmol_gDM
  ~ .x * (100/percent.C),   # multiply by (100/percent.C)
  .names = "{.col}_scaled")) %>%   # name the new column pigment_scaled
  rename_with(~ sub("_nmol_gDM_scaled$", "_nmol_gTC", .x), ends_with("_scaled"))
  # rename all scaled columns (and not the original columns) with new unit

TRK_wide <- TRK_wide %>%
  mutate(across(ends_with("_nmol_gDM"), 
  ~ .x * (100/percent.C), 
  .names = "{.col}_scaled")) %>%
  rename_with(~ sub("_nmol_gDM_scaled$", "_nmol_gTC", .x), ends_with("_scaled"))

LFM_wide <- LFM_wide %>%
  mutate(across(ends_with("_nmol_gDM"), 
  ~ .x * (100/percent.C), 
  .names = "{.col}_scaled")) %>%
  rename_with(~ sub("_nmol_gDM_scaled$", "_nmol_gTC", .x), ends_with("_scaled"))

```

Decide which of the pigments to analyze and which to set aside: 

**Pigments missing from every core:** chlide_a, chl_c1, chl_c2, peridinin, sed_a, sed_b, sed_c, oscil, aphan, viola, diadino, myxo, zea, okenone, isoren, a_car, car_x, car_y, car_z

**pigments in every core:** *fuco (drops off in TRK)*, allo, diato, lutein, *cantha (none in TRK)*, chl_b, chl_a, chl_ap, echine, phaeo_b, pheo_a, b_car.

**Pigments focused on in bella's paper:** 
allo, diato, lutein, *cantha*, *myxo*, *zea*, echine, phaeo_b, pheo_a, b_car

**Missing from my data, in Bellas:** myxo, zea, cantha (none in TRK), diadino 

**Consider later:** 
- why is there no diadino? what does that say about diatoms given [diato]...?
- these cores were ~9 months old when analyzed (and experienced more freeze-thaw cycles than is ideal): what do the preservation indices tell us about the reliability of the values we obtained, and/or the many zeroes. 
- how can you assess the extent of post-depositional degradation of a given pigment? 
- interpret AD ratio? perc_chlb, etc.
- compare pigments in cyanos with those in vascular plants? no. Per Peter most chl degrades by the time it reaches the water column. 

**Remove from short dfs:** chlide_a, chl_c1, chl_c2, peridinin, sed_a, sed_b, sed_c, oscil, aphan, viola, diadino, myxo, zea, okenone, isoren, a_car, car_x, car_y, car_z

### Clean up each df, add summary pigment metrics
```{r}
TRK_short <- TRK_wide %>% # make a new subset df with variables of interest
  select(-ends_with("_gDM"), # remove pigments with g / dry mass unit
         -chlide_a_nmol_gTC, # remove pigments with 0 values 
         -chl_c1_nmol_gTC,
         -chl_c2_nmol_gTC, 
         -perid_nmol_gTC, 
         -sed_a_nmol_gTC, 
         -sed_b_nmol_gTC, 
         -sed_c_nmol_gTC, 
         -oscil_nmol_gTC, 
         -aphan_nmol_gTC, 
         -viola_nmol_gTC, 
         -diadino_nmol_gTC, 
         -myxo_nmol_gTC, 
         -zea_nmol_gTC,
         -okenone_nmol_gTC, 
         -isoren_nmol_gTC, 
         -a_car_nmol_gTC,
         -car_x_nmol_gTC,
         -car_y_nmol_gTC, 
         -car_z_nmol_gTC) %>%
  mutate(chla_pheoa = chl_a_nmol_gTC + pheo_a_nmol_gTC, # add new columns with summary metrics
         chls = chl_a_nmol_gTC + pheo_a_nmol_gTC + chl_ap_nmol_gTC, 
         chlb_pheob = chl_b_nmol_gTC + phaeo_b_nmol_gTC,
         all_chl = chl_a_nmol_gTC + pheo_a_nmol_gTC + chl_ap_nmol_gTC, 
         # no chlide, chl_c1 or chl_c2 in any core
         # all_diat = diato_nmol_gTC + diadino_nmol_gTC; not calculated - NO DIADINO
         PI = chl_a_nmol_gTC/pheo_a_nmol_gTC, # preservation index
         # UVR_index = sed_c_nmol_gTC / (allo_nmol_gTC + diato_nmol_gTC+lutein_nmol_gTC)
         # UVR not calculated, no sed C in any core
         AD_ratio = allo_nmol_gTC / diato_nmol_gTC, 
         master_chl = (chl_a_nmol_gTC + chl_b_nmol_gTC) / (chl_ap_nmol_gTC + pheo_a_nmol_gTC + phaeo_b_nmol_gTC),
         perc_chlb = (phaeo_b_nmol_gTC / pheo_a_nmol_gTC), 
         greens = phaeo_b_nmol_gTC + lutein_nmol_gTC,
         cyanos = cantha_nmol_gTC + echine_nmol_gTC,
         perc_diatox = (diato_nmol_gTC/chla_pheoa))

# repeat for UFM
UFM_short <- UFM_wide %>% 
  select(-ends_with("_gDM"), 
         -chlide_a_nmol_gTC, 
         -chl_c1_nmol_gTC,
         -chl_c2_nmol_gTC, 
         -perid_nmol_gTC, 
         -sed_a_nmol_gTC, 
         -sed_b_nmol_gTC, 
         -sed_c_nmol_gTC, 
         -oscil_nmol_gTC, 
         -aphan_nmol_gTC, 
         -viola_nmol_gTC, 
         -diadino_nmol_gTC, 
         -myxo_nmol_gTC, 
         -zea_nmol_gTC,
         -okenone_nmol_gTC, 
         -isoren_nmol_gTC, 
         -a_car_nmol_gTC,
         -car_x_nmol_gTC,
         -car_y_nmol_gTC, 
         -car_z_nmol_gTC) %>%
  mutate(chla_pheoa = chl_a_nmol_gTC + pheo_a_nmol_gTC, 
         chlb_pheob = chl_b_nmol_gTC + phaeo_b_nmol_gTC,
         chls = chl_a_nmol_gTC + pheo_a_nmol_gTC + chl_ap_nmol_gTC,
         all_chl = chl_a_nmol_gTC + pheo_a_nmol_gTC + chl_ap_nmol_gTC,

         perc_chlb = (phaeo_b_nmol_gTC / pheo_a_nmol_gTC),
```

```{r}
  relocate(chla_pheoa:last_col(), .after = car_z_nmol_gTC)
```

### Evaluate preservation index
```{r}
# quickly visualize chl_a and PI, if PI spikes (past 1) near the surface (depth = 0 cm), increases in Chl_a near depth 0 may be suspect / preservation effects may be significant. 

ggplot(UFM_short, aes(x = depth_top, y = chl_a_nmol_gTC)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, color = "darkgreen", na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_line(color = "darkgreen", na.rm = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "Upper Fourmile",
    x = "Depth top (cm)",
    y = "Chl-a (nmol/gTC)") + 
  theme_minimal()

ggplot(UFM_short, aes(x = depth_top, y = PI)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, color = "darkgreen", na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_line(color = "darkgreen", na.rm = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "Upper Fourmile",
    x = "Depth top (cm)",
    y = "Preservation Index") +
  theme_minimal()

ggplot(TRK_short, aes(x = depth_top, y = chl_a_nmol_gTC)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, color = "steelblue", na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", na.rm = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "Turkey Creek",
    x = "Depth top (cm)",
    y = "Chl-a (nmol/gTC)") +
  theme_minimal()

ggplot(TRK_short, aes(x = depth_top, y = PI)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, color = "steelblue", na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", na.rm = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "Turkey Creek",
    x = "Depth top (cm)",
    y = "Preservation Index") +
  theme_minimal()

```

# Date Interpolation (Pb-210 data)

### Pull in dates (UFM and LFM)
```{r}
### ADM (age-depth model) method adapted from Cale Gushulak's scripts (see cales_code)

### read in the chronology data from Flett to pull into the adms
all_dates <- read_excel("data/Flett_dates_simplified_20250917.xlsx")
# (this spreadsheet was compiled using the three final Pb-210 reports sent by Flett). 

    # (depth top and bottom correspond to the depth of each sample in the core. 
    # sed accumulation rates were extrapolated (by Flett) for sections of the core 
    # (between the samples tested) using the Pb-210 activities and bulk density values 
    # of the samples analyzed. Ages were then calculated for the bottom of each extrapolated 
    # section.using the linear, CRS, or combined method. 

# Split the chronology data by lake:

UFM_dates <- all_dates %>%
    filter(str_starts(sample_ID, "UFM")) %>% # select only the UFM rows
    #join, removing columns depth top and bottom before pulling in UFM_metadata
    left_join(UFM_metadata %>% select(-depth_top, -depth_bottom), 
              by = "sample_ID") %>% # join by sample_ID
    relocate(all_of(c(names(UFM_metadata)))) %>%
    # keep columns in the same order as in the metadata doc.
    mutate(year_CE = 2025 - extrap_bottom_age_lin)
       # calculate year by substracting the sample age from the year of analysis. 
       # NOTE !!!
       # AGES CORRESPOND TO EXTRAP BOTTOM!!
       # UFM ages derived from the linear model!

# repeat for LFM
LFM_dates <- all_dates %>%
      filter(str_starts(sample_ID, "LFM")) %>%
      left_join(LFM_metadata %>% select(-depth_top, -depth_bottom),
                by = "sample_ID") %>%
      relocate(all_of(c(names(LFM_metadata)))) %>%
      mutate(year_CE = 2025 - extrap_bottom_age_CRS)
         # NOTE !!!
         # AGES CORRESPOND TO EXTRAP BOTTOM!
         # LFM ages derived from CRS (simple)

```


### TRK (raw data -> adm)
```{r}
# TRK disaster summary (see Flett's report for more detail):

# the bd and Pb-210 values of sections 10 - 27 cm of core TRK2 suggest potential import of 
# foreign sediments to the coring site. This would violate the assumptions of the CRS model. 
# To compensate, Flett computationally removed these sections and reassigned depths for 
# samples TRK2_058 and TRK2_082 (from lower depths 29 to 12 and 40.5 to 24, respectively).
# Flett then estimated depths for the reconstructed cores using a linear regression.

# Regardless of the values provided through the linear regression for the reconstructed core, 
# Xiaoxi wrote us that "sections in between 058 and 082 cannot be reliably dated. 

# In order to estimate SOME age for plotting purposes ONLY, we assumed a constant sedimentation
# rate between the lowest unchanged sample of the original core (TRK2_020) and the bottom 
# sample of the core (reconstructed lower depth = 24, original = 41 cm). In the code below, 
# this means an adm is constructed for TRK using an adjusted TRK_dates df, where row TRK2_058 
# is removed, and the extrapolated bottom depth of sample TRK2_082 is readjusted to its 
# original, rather than reconstructed value (= 41cm).

TRK_dates <- all_dates %>% 
        filter(str_starts(sample_ID, "TRK")) %>% # filter for TRK rows 
        left_join(TRK_metadata %>% select(-depth_top, -depth_bottom), # combine w the metadata
                  by = "sample_ID") %>%
        relocate(all_of(c(names(TRK_metadata)))) %>%
        mutate(year_CE = 2025 - extrap_bottom_age_CRS) %>% # calculate sample deposition years
        # remove row TRK2_058 from the df (so it doesn't go into the adm)
        filter(!sample_ID %in% c("TRK2_058")) %>%  
        # replace extrap bottom depth from the value in the reconstructed core 
        # to the value in the original core.
        mutate(extrap_top = if_else(sample_ID == "TRK2_082", NA, extrap_top),
               extrap_bottom = if_else(sample_ID == "TRK2_082", 41, extrap_bottom))
    
      # NOTE 
      # AGES CORRESPOND TO EXTRAP BOTTOM
      # TRK ages come from lin-derived CRS
  
TRK_adm <- age_depth_model(TRK_dates, 
                           depth = extrap_bottom,
                           age = year_CE)

plot(TRK_adm)
# CHECK: looks good The adm  assumes a constant rate of sedimentation between 10 and 41 cm 
# in the core, based on the age estimate provided for the bottom of sample TRK2_082. 
# ages beyond 10 cm are for plotting purposes only, and above are "GROSS APPROXIMATIONS ONLY". 
```

```{r}
# create adm, using the date that corresponds to depth EXTRAP_bottom
UFM_adm <- age_depth_model(UFM_dates_clean,
                           depth = extrap_bottom,

# visualize adm

     xlab="Depth (cm)",
```

### Interpolate dates & join to dfs

#### TRK
```{r}
### Calculate year deposited for the top, bottom, and center of each sample based on 
  # the age-depth relationships defined for sections of the core in the adm. 

  # btwn the dated samples is interpolation, beyond (above and below!) is extrapolation. 

   # (rounded) lowest extrap_bottom value for each core: 
      # UFM: 5 cm
      # LFM: 18 cm
      # TRK: 11 cm (10.75)

# make a df to hold interpolated / extrapolated ages
TRK_interp <- predict(TRK_adm, depth = seq(0.25, 41, 0.25)) %>% # 0.25 cm increments = top, 
  # bottom, and center
  mutate(year_CE = age) %>% # adm calls this age but its really a year
  select(depth, year_CE) # the adm program labels interpolated vs. extrapolated but we don't 
  # need that here. 

# NOTE: SWITCHING HERE FROM EXTRAP_BOTTOM TO REGULAR depth_bottom

## Rearrange the interp df so depths ending in _.5, _.75, and _.0 can be categorized as sample
# depth_top, depth_plot, and depth_bottom. (we don't care about 0.25 bc of the arrangement of 
# samples we happened to analyze for SIA & pigments). 

  # define functions to categorize depths by ending digits
  is_whole  <- function(x, tol = 1e-8) abs(x %% 1) < tol
  is_half   <- function(x, tol = 1e-8) abs(x %% 1 - 0.5) < tol
  is_three_quarters <- function(x, tol = 1e-8) abs(x %% 1 - 0.75) < tol
  
  # make new columns copying depth into the correct category (top, plot, or bottom)
  TRK_interp <- TRK_interp %>%
    mutate(
      depth_top    = ifelse(is_half(depth), depth, NA_real_),
      depth_plot   = ifelse(is_three_quarters(depth), depth, NA_real_),
      depth_bottom = ifelse(is_whole(depth), depth, NA_real_)
    ) %>%
    select(depth, year_CE, depth_top, depth_plot, depth_bottom)

# Join the new columns to TRK_wide by depth: top, plot, then bottom
TRK_wide <- TRK_wide %>%
  left_join(
    TRK_interp %>% 
      select(depth_top, year_CE) %>%
      rename(year_CE_top = year_CE),
    by = "depth_top")

TRK_wide <- TRK_wide %>%
  left_join(
    TRK_interp %>% 
      select(depth_plot, year_CE) %>%
      rename(year_CE_plot = year_CE),
    by = "depth_plot")

TRK_wide <- TRK_wide %>%
  left_join(
    TRK_interp %>% 
      select(depth_bottom, year_CE) %>%
      rename(year_CE_bottom = year_CE),
    by = "depth_bottom") 

# this is a little circular but I actually want the TRK dfs in the same format as UFM and LFM
# the more detailed ages are for calculating mass accumulation rates, and we only care about
# these where the ages are somewhat accurate. So, copy year_CE_plot over and name it 
# year_plot_extrap (this provides year_CE_plot for every sample). then trim year_CE_plot, top, 
# and bottom so they are NA past the end of the more reliably dated region. Also create a 
# column called duration (years represented by that 0.5 cm sample). 

TRK_wide <- TRK_wide %>%
  mutate(
    duration = if_else(year_CE_plot > 1980, year_CE_top - year_CE_bottom, NA_real_),
    year_plot_extrap = year_CE_plot,
    across(
      c(year_CE_plot, year_CE_top, year_CE_bottom),
      ~ if_else(is.na(duration), NA_real_, .)))
      
# Also add a weight term to TRK_wide (need to do this separately because of how mutate groups)
# weights can be used to differentially weight samples in the GAM so samples that encompass 
# more time matter more to the model. But, see gavin simpson 2018 - you need to normalize 
# weight against the mean(weight) to avoid changing the model likelihood so the weights don't 
# affect the model likelihood (and you can compare across methods). 

duration_mean_TRK <- mean(TRK_wide$duration, na.rm = TRUE)
TRK_wide <- mutate(TRK_wide, weight = duration / duration_mean_TRK)

# Repeat for TRK_short
TRK_short <- TRK_short %>%
  left_join(
    TRK_wide %>%
      ungroup() %>% # keep R from adding these variables twice
      select(sample_ID, year_CE_top:weight), 
    by = "sample_ID")

# names(TRK_short)
# View(TRK_wide %>% select(lake_name:bd, year_CE_top:weight))

### NOTE! extrapolated ages for the nondated cores are calculated for UFM and LFM in the file
# 02a_date_extrapolation. Here dates are only interpolated for those cores. 
```

```{r}
# NB: this was just an exercise in interpolating instantaneous sediment accumulation rates, 
# not ultimately used for thesis but basis for calculating mass flux.  

# sit down with a pen for this part... 
TRK_short <- TRK_short %>%
  mutate(s = (bd*0.5)/duration)

# check that I can get the same answer as Flett (once from a core with CRS dating and once 
# from a core with the lin regression)
# I think the mismatch is coming from the fact that accumulation rate is calculated for the 
# extrapolated section. let's check on TRK2_004: 

# sed accumulation rate (CRS) = 0.0291
# my est improved: 0.02792188 (~4% diff)
# my estimate: 0.02463377 (not exact...)

# TRK2_001: 0.139
# TRK2_003 corresponds to bd = 0.12656729
# TRK2_005: 0.115

# TRK2_003 represents 0.75 to 2.25cm, or 1 - 1.5
# extrap = 
(0.139*0.25+0.127*0.5+(2.25-1.5)*0.113) / (2022.359 - 2015.805)
  
  # Flett "mass in extrapolated section" column is wrong? misestimates the mass depth... 

    # this is what they did instead (assign bd of given depth to whole extrapolated section...)
    (0.127*(2.25-0.75))/(2022.359 - 2015.805) # = 0.02906622
```

#Mass flux 
### %C and %N calculations
```{r}
# calculate mass flux (mass accumulation rates, mar) for C and N

# add a column to TRK_short and TRK_wide with nutrient flux. C.mar after percent.C and N.mar 
# after percent.N. 

TRK_short <- TRK_short %>%
  mutate(
    C.mar = (percent.C / 100) * s,
    N.mar = (percent.N / 100) * s) %>%
  relocate(C.mar, .after = percent.C) %>%
  relocate(N.mar, .after = percent.N)

TRK_wide <- TRK_wide %>%
  mutate(
    C.mar = (percent.C / 100) * s,
    N.mar = (percent.N / 100) * s) %>%
  relocate(C.mar, .after = percent.C) %>%
  relocate(N.mar, .after = percent.N)

# Repeat for UFM
UFM_short <- UFM_short %>%
  mutate(
    C.mar = (percent.C / 100) * s,
    N.mar = (percent.N / 100) * s) %>%
  relocate(C.mar, .after = percent.C) %>%
  relocate(N.mar, .after = percent.N)

UFM_wide <- UFM_wide %>%
  mutate(
    C.mar = (percent.C / 100) * s,
    N.mar = (percent.N / 100) * s) %>%
  relocate(C.mar, .after = percent.C) %>%
  relocate(N.mar, .after = percent.N)

# Repeat for LFM
LFM_short <- LFM_short %>%
  mutate(
    C.mar = (percent.C / 100) * s,
    N.mar = (percent.N / 100) * s) %>%
  relocate(C.mar, .after = percent.C) %>%
  relocate(N.mar, .after = percent.N)

LFM_wide <- LFM_wide %>%
  mutate(
    C.mar = (percent.C / 100) * s,
    N.mar = (percent.N / 100) * s) %>%
  relocate(C.mar, .after = percent.C) %>%
  relocate(N.mar, .after = percent.N)
```

```{r}
  ggplot(aes(x=depth_top, y=value, color=name))+
  geom_point()+
  geom_line()+
  geom_smooth(method="gam")+ # "really easy to plot a gam"
  facet_wrap(.~name, scales="free_y")+
  theme(legend.position="none")

UFM_short %>%
  pivot_longer(d13C:perc_diatox) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=depth_top, y=value, color=name))+
  geom_point()+
  geom_line()+
  facet_wrap(.~name, scales="free_y")+
  theme(legend.position="none")

LFM_short %>%
  pivot_longer(d13C:perc_diatox) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=depth_top, y=value, color=name))+
  geom_point()+
  geom_line()+
  facet_wrap(.~name, scales="free_y")+
  theme(legend.position="none")
```

# Export
```{r}
# Combine all lakes into one data frame
all_lakes <- bind_rows(UFM_short, LFM_short, TRK_short)

# export important dfs as csvs 
write.csv(all_lakes, file="output/all_lakes.csv")
write.csv(LFM_wide, file="output/LFM_wide.csv")
write.csv(UFM_wide, file="output/UFM_wide.csv")
write.csv(TRK_wide, file="output/TRK_wide.csv")
write.csv(LFM_short, file="output/LFM_short.csv")
write.csv(UFM_short, file="output/UFM_short.csv")
write.csv(TRK_short, file="output/TRK_short.csv")

# save the age-depth models too
saveRDS(UFM_adm, "output/UFM_adm.rds")
saveRDS(LFM_adm, "output/LFM_adm.rds")
saveRDS(TRK_adm, "output/TRK_adm.rds")
```
